req.title: Return GET request metadata
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /get with a JSON object containing the request's URL, headers, arguments, and origin IP.
expected_outcomes: JSON body with keys url, args, headers, origin
error_pathways: HTTP 405 if a non-GET method is used

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET /get returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing exactly the keys 'url', 'args', 'headers', and 'origin'. Error pathway requires HTTP 405 for non-GET methods. Tests cover: (1) positive EP – plain GET returns 200 with all four required keys present and non-null; (2) positive EP – query string args are reflected exactly in the 'args' key; (3) negative NEG – POST to /get returns 405 (method not allowed); (4) negative NEG – PUT to /get returns 405; (5) boundary BVA – GET with zero query params yields empty args dict (not None, not missing); (6) boundary BVA – GET with multiple query params yields all reflected; (7) DT – custom request header is reflected in the 'headers' sub-object. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_get_returns_200_with_required_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
No special headers or query params
actions: Issue GET /get with no query parameters
expected: JSON body contains exactly the keys: url, args, headers, origin
None of those four values is None
trace: R-HTTPBIN-001 – Expected outcomes: JSON body with keys url, args, headers, origin; HTTP 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_returns_200_with_required_keys():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'application/json' in r.content_type
    data = r.get_json()
    assert set(data.keys()) >= {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin'}
    assert data['url'] is not None
    assert data['args'] is not None
    assert data['headers'] is not None
    assert data['origin'] is not None

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_reflects_custom_header_in_headers_key():
    r = client.get('/get', headers={'X-Test-Header': 'sentinel-value'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert 'headers' in data
    headers_lower = {k.lower(): v for k, v in data['headers'].items()}
    assert headers_lower.get('x-test-header') == 'sentinel-value'
